conecta.name: Connect the colours
conecta.intro: Draw a path between each pair of matching colours. The paths share a board, so a route that works for one pair can cut off another.
conecta.tip: Look for a pair that must pass through a narrow gap. Reserve that gap before drawing a line for a colour with more room.
conecta.challenge: A red pair can go around the edge or through a gap in the centre. The blue pair can only use the gap. Where should the red line go?
conecta.answer: Take red around the edge and leave the gap for blue. That way both pairs can still connect.

numeros.name: Connect the numbers
numeros.searchTitle: Connect the Numbers – Free Online Number Path Puzzle
numeros.intro: Play a free number path puzzle online. Connect the numbered squares in order without stepping on the same square twice. Can you leave a path to the last number?
numeros.tip: Before you connect 2 to 3, find 4. Leave yourself a way out of 3 that doesn’t cross the path you just drew.
numeros.challenge: From 2 you can reach 3 along the border or through the centre. The centre is the only way from 3 to 4. Which route should you take first?
numeros.answer: Take the border from 2 to 3. The central square will still be free when you need it to reach 4.

calculo.name: Mental maths challenge
calculo.intro: Work out the answer to each calculation and choose it on screen. The difficulty ranges from basic arithmetic to percentages and multi-step sums.
calculo.tip: For 39 + 16, try 40 + 16 and take one away. The same trick works whenever a number is close to a multiple of ten.
calculo.challenge: You need 48 + 27. How could you reach the next ten before finishing the sum?
calculo.answer: Split 27 into 2 and 25. Add 2 to 48 to reach 50, then add 25 to get 75.

palabras.name: Word scramble
palabras.intro: Use the clue to work out the hidden word, then put the scrambled letters in order. Your answer has to fit both the clue and the letters on screen.
palabras.tip: Think of two possible answers to the clue. Count the letters and see which one you can actually build.
palabras.challenge: The letters are R, A and E. The clue says ‘the part of your body you use to hear’. Which word fits?
palabras.answer: EAR. ARE uses the same letters, but it doesn’t fit the clue.

sopa.name: Word search
sopa.intro: Find the words from the list hidden in a grid of letters. Each puzzle has a theme, from nature and sport to science and technology.
sopa.tip: Choose a word with an unusual letter. Find that letter in the grid, then check its neighbours for the rest of the word.
sopa.challenge: You are looking for LION. One row reads K L I O N E. Which letters do you mark?
sopa.answer: Start at L, the second letter, and continue to N, the fifth. Those four cells spell LION in order.

sudoku.name: Mini Sudoku
sudoku.intro: Fill a 4×4 or 6×6 grid so each number appears once in every row, column and block. Try three difficulty levels with a limited supply of hints.
sudoku.tip: In a 4×4 row containing 1, 2 and 4, the empty square needs a 3. Check its column and block to confirm the move.
sudoku.challenge: A row of a 4×4 puzzle reads 2, empty, 4, 3. Which number belongs in the empty square?
sudoku.answer: 1. It is the only number from 1 to 4 missing from that row.

memoria.name: Memory matching game
memoria.intro: Turn over two cards at a time and look for matching pictures. When two different pictures turn up, their positions become clues for later turns.
memoria.tip: Give each new picture a location as you see it, such as ‘star, top left’. That gives you somewhere to go when its twin appears.
memoria.challenge: Earlier you turned over a bicycle in the bottom left. You have just found a bicycle in the top right. Which card do you turn next?
memoria.answer: Choose the bottom-left card. The remembered position lets you match the two bicycles.

series.name: Number sequence puzzles
series.intro: Find the rule behind a sequence of numbers and choose what comes next. The pattern might involve a steady increase, a multiplier or two sequences taking turns.
series.tip: If consecutive numbers seem unrelated, read the first, third and fifth together. Then try the second, fourth and sixth.
series.challenge: What follows 2, 9, 4, 8, 6, 7 if the two alternating patterns continue?
series.answer: 8. The numbers in positions 1, 3 and 5 go up by two: 2, 4, 6. The other numbers count down from 9.

crucigrama.name: Crossword puzzles
crucigrama.intro: Read each clue and fit its answer into the grid. Where two words cross, a single letter has to work for both answers.
crucigrama.tip: Fill in a clue you know, then try the words that cross it. Check the length of each answer before committing to it.
crucigrama.challenge: The clue is ‘a planet called the Red Planet’. Your four squares read M, blank, R, S. Which letter belongs in the gap?
crucigrama.answer: A completes MARS. The answer also gives you an A for the word that crosses the gap.

tiempo.name: Beat the clock quiz
tiempo.intro: Take on ten short, timed challenges. A maths problem can be followed by a word question, a logic puzzle or a test of attention.
tiempo.tip: Read the instruction on each new screen first. The previous question might have asked for a number while this one asks for a word.
tiempo.challenge: One timed question asks for 7 + 5. The next asks which word names a colour: ‘eight’, ‘blue’ or ‘high’. What are the two answers?
tiempo.answer: 12, then blue. Read the instruction on the second screen before you look for another number.

verdadero.name: True or false quiz
verdadero.intro: Decide whether a statement is true or false, then read the explanation. The questions range across maths, language, science and technology.
verdadero.tip: When a statement says ‘always’ or ‘never’, try to think of one exception before you choose.
verdadero.challenge: True or false: every multiple of 2 is also a multiple of 4.
verdadero.answer: False. Six is a multiple of 2, but 6 cannot be divided evenly by 4.

cocomed.name: Coco Med: human body and health quiz
cocomed.intro: Explore anatomy, nutrition and everyday health habits through quiz questions. Read the explanation after each answer to see how the idea works.
cocomed.tip: When a question introduces an organ, say its job in your own words. For example, the heart pumps blood through the body.
cocomed.challenge: Which organ pumps blood around the body: the heart or the lungs?
cocomed.answer: The heart pumps blood. The lungs allow oxygen to move from the air into the blood.

futbol.name: Football goal memory game
futbol.intro: Watch different sections of a football goal light up in sequence. When the lights stop, shoot at the section that stayed dark.
futbol.tip: Name the corners as they light up. At the end, check which position is missing from your list.
futbol.challenge: Three corners of the goal flashed: top left, bottom right and bottom left. Which corner stayed dark?
futbol.answer: Top right. Aim there once the sequence ends.

padel.name: Padel tournament organiser
padel.intro: Set up the players, courts and rounds for a padel session you play in person. Enter match results to follow your group’s standings.
padel.tip: Agree on round length and scoring before anyone takes the court. Enter each score while the players still remember it.
padel.challenge: Eight players want to play doubles on two courts. How many players can play in the same round?
padel.answer: All eight. A doubles match uses four players per court, so two courts hold eight players.

bank.name: Coco Bank: virtual money budgeting game
bank.intro: Manage a virtual account, cover household expenses and save towards a goal. Use the money left over to explore simulated investments.
bank.tip: Set aside the next bill before choosing an investment. If you have 100 and owe 60, base your next decision on the remaining 40.
bank.challenge: Your virtual balance is 100. You need 60 for expenses and want to save 25. How much is left for something else?
bank.answer: 15 units of game money. Deduct both the bills and your savings: 100 − 60 − 25 = 15.

ciudad.name: Coco City board game
ciudad.intro: Roll the die and explore a 40-space city board with two to six players, on a shared device or in a private online room. Landing on a space can bring a property or a choice about city life.
ciudad.tip: Before buying a property, work out what you would have left afterwards and check whether the purchase helps your current goal.
ciudad.challenge: A property costs 90 and you have 100 in game money. You want to keep 25 for another goal. Can you do both now?
ciudad.answer: No. The purchase would leave you with 10. To keep 25 for your goal, you could spend at most 75.

generala.name: Generala dice game
generala.intro: Roll five dice up to three times per turn, keeping the dice you want between rolls. Choose one of the eleven categories on your scorecard for your result.
generala.tip: With three fours, check whether your fours category or four of a kind is still open. That can change which dice are worth rolling again.
generala.challenge: On your first roll you get 4, 4, 4, 2 and 5. Your fours category is open. What could you score immediately?
generala.answer: 12 in fours. You can also keep the three fours and roll the other two dice again to try for a bigger combination.

naval.name: Battleships
naval.intro: Hide five ships on a 10×10 grid and take turns firing one shot at the opposing fleet. Play against Coco or invite a friend to a private online room.
naval.tip: After two hits in a line, try the squares at either end. Ships can touch in this version, so a square next to a sunken ship can still hold another one.
naval.challenge: You hit D4 and D5, and the ship is still afloat. Which untried squares extend that line?
naval.answer: D3 and D6. Fire at one end first. If those hits belong to the same ship, it must run along that row.

truco.name: Argentine Truco card game
truco.intro: Play Argentine Truco against Coco or with friends at tables for two, four or six. Choose a target of 15 or 30 points and play with envido and truco, without flor.
truco.tip: Check for two cards of the same suit before calling envido. A six and a seven of the same suit are worth 33 together: 20 plus their two values.
truco.challenge: You hold the six and seven of coins and a king of cups. How many points can you claim for envido?
truco.answer: 33. The six and seven share a suit, so you add 20 to their values: 20 + 6 + 7.

ajedrez.name: Online chess
ajedrez.intro: Play chess against Coco, share a board on one device or meet another registered player in an online room. There are also lessons, challenges and a daily game.
ajedrez.tip: Before moving a defender, check which piece it currently protects. Picture your opponent’s best reply to the move you have in mind.
ajedrez.challenge: Your king is in check from a knight. Can you escape by putting another piece between them?
ajedrez.answer: No. A knight jumps, so its check cannot be blocked. You need a legal king move or a legal capture of the attacking knight.
